subject: Dry run kickoff: evidence ingest & QC for vendor security profiles
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dry run kickoff: evidence ingest & QC for vendor security profiles

Hi Jessica —

Thanks again for agreeing to a short dry run to validate the evidence ingest process into Whistic/Vendr before we do the full handoff. Goal: exercise the full flow (manifest -> upload -> profile attachment -> QC) so we can catch mapping and access issues ahead of the production drop.

Proposed scope for the dry run (attached checklist + small manifest):
- 10 representative documents (PDF, txt log, S3-hosted syslog sample)
- CAIQ + SIG mapping tags (we'll include the CAIQ question IDs in the manifest)
- Upload using pre-signed S3 URLs from your side (we'll provide target object keys)
- QC: filename normalization, hash verification, and evidence link rendering in Whistic

I attached: whistic-dryrun-checklist.xlsx and ingest-sample-manifest.csv.
Can you confirm: 1) you can provide pre-signed PUT URLs for a temporary read-only bucket; 2) your SRE allows inbound requests from our pipeline IPs (I included them in the Drive doc).

Suggested window: Tue 11 May, 09:00–10:30 PT (we'll be on the call to coordinate). If that doesn't work, propose alternatives.

Next steps after confirmation: internal runbook execution, quick QC pass, and a short follow-up to capture remediation items.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: whistic-dryrun-checklist.xlsx (14KB), ingest-sample-manifest.csv (2KB)

From: Jessica Simms <jessica.simms@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dry run kickoff: evidence ingest & QC for vendor security profiles

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear plan and the checklist. We can do a dry run but a couple of clarifications before locking the time: 1) our security team prefers to generate the pre-signed URLs and hand them to you (they won’t accept inbound PUT requests from unknown IPs); 2) the S3 bucket will be temporary but must have ACLs set to internal-only until you confirm manifest mapping; 3) for CAIQ mapping, can you include the question ID column in the manifest (we need that to finalize evidence relationships automatically).

We can make Tue 11 May 09:00 PT work but prefer to run the upload step immediately after the call so we can observe the object keys and confirm hashes. I’ll create a short calendar invite and include our SRE on the call.

One minor ask: do you have a sample expected Whistic metadata JSON for each file (we want to pre-map tags client-side)? If you can drop that in the Drive link you shared, our onboarding engineer can pre-attach in the staging profile.

—Jessica
Jessica Simms
Head of Vendor Security, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com | +1 (617) 555-0824

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 12:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dry run kickoff: evidence ingest & QC for vendor security profiles

Jessica —

Great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick responses inline: 1) Works fine — we'll consume your pre-signed PUT URLs; please scope them to the temporary bucket path we listed in the Drive doc (folder: /whistic-dryrun/acme/). 2) ACLs: understood — we only need read access after upload for verification; we will not change bucket policies. 3) Manifest: the attached CSV includes a CAIQ_ID column, but I’ll also drop a sample Whistic metadata JSON in the Drive folder by EOD (filename: whistic-sample-metadata.json).

Agenda for Tue 11 May 09:00 PT (30–45 min):
- Quick alignment on manifest column semantics (Ben) — 10 min
- SRE: deliver pre-signed URLs (Acme) — 5 min
- Upload step (Acme engineer) — 10–15 min
- QC: hash check + verify in staging profile (Karthik / Marissa) — 10 min
- Capture follow-ups and remediation items — 5 min

We’ll be prepared to run the lightweight QC and note any mapping or rendering issues in the profile. Karthik, can you confirm we have the ingest script and sample manifest validator ready? Marissa, can you own the Whistic staging checks and take screenshots for the post-run notes?

Ben

On a related note: I added the HubSpot record HS-23456 to the related links so our CRM shows the kickoff activity for the account.

Attachments: none (drive uploads incoming).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jessica Simms <jessica.simms@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 22:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dry run kickoff: evidence ingest & QC for vendor security profiles

Folks —

Quick post-run update from our side after the Tue session (ran the ingest at ~10:20 PT):
- Ingest: consumed Acme pre-signed URLs successfully; manifest parsing OK.
- QC findings: 1) two filenames contained non-UTF8 characters causing a render gap in Whistic — we normalized to underscores and re-linked; 2) one PDF had an embedded font that prevented text extraction (flagged as image-only evidence) — noted under remediation item #2 in the Drive doc; 3) CAIQ mapping worked for the sample set, but we need to extend the manifest to include alternate question synonyms to cover clients that use non-standard nomenclature.

Deliverables (what I uploaded to the shared Drive):
- ingest-run-log-20270511.txt (hashes, timings, HTTP status codes)
- whistic-qc-screenshots.zip (screenshots of rendered evidence in staging)
- remediation-items.md (short list with owner assignments)

Next steps:
- Marissa to run a second quick pass on the Whistic profile to confirm the normalized filenames render correctly (Marissa: can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?).
- Ben: ask Acme if they can include a UTF-8 filename normalization step on their client-side export (two small changes).
- I'll draft a short runbook update incorporating the filename normalization and image-only evidence handling.

Overall the dry run reduced unknowns — upload flow and mapping look solid. We captured a small remediation list and a quick follow-up plan.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer | Security Engineering
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments uploaded to Drive: ingest-run-log-20270511.txt, whistic-qc-screenshots.zip, remediation-items.md
